newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada mulls NAFTA challenge of U.S. sugar policy.
newsitem.headline: Canada mulls NAFTA challenge of U.S. sugar policy.

text.p: Canada may resort to a North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) challenge of the U.S. program for re-export of sugar-containing products if talks next month fail to resolve a dispute between the two countries, an Agriculture Canada spokesman said on Thursday.

According to the Canadian sugar industry, Washington had agreed under NAFTA to scrap the re-export program for sugar containing products on January 1, 1996, but had failed to do so, despite protests from Ottawa.
Vern Greenshields, spokesman for Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale, said Canada would bring up the issue at a NAFTA commission meeting next month.
Following the meeting, Washington would have 30 days to respond and scrap the program or face a NAFTA challenge from Canada.
"If that process doesn't result in a resolution, then we will be going to that next stage," Greenshields said.

Canadian manufacturers of sugar-containing products claim that under the U.S. program they face increasing imports of U.S. products which normally would not be competitive because of Canada's lower sugar costs.

"U.S. exports have quadrupled and the situation is expected to get worse as Canadian tariffs are eliminated by 1998 under the NAFTA," the Canadian Sugar Institute, a sugar industry lobby group, said in a press release. ((Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau, 613-235-6745))
